newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Barlows sees difficult year ahead.
newsitem.headline: Barlows sees difficult year ahead.

text.p: Industrial group Barlow Ltd said on Monday that a slowdown in fixed investment spending in South Africa pointed to continued difficult domestic trading conditions for much of the year ahead.
However, the company said its businesses were well managed and capitalised and well placed to respond to any pick-up in the market.

The international operations would continue to benefit from growing economies. Overall, earnings for 1997 should show real growth, the company said in a statement with results for the year to September 30.
"Our companies are in good shape and are ready to run should the economy and market conditions allow us to do so," said chairman Warren Clewlow.
Barlows said its overseas units had kicked in a strong performance in the year to September, with 25 percent of attributable profit earned in foreign currency against 20 percent a year ago.

Foreign-based subsidiaries' contribution to attributable profit was up 59 perent in rand terms. Capital equipment and northern hemisphere industrial companies contributed strongly, as did materials handling equipment. A loss was incurred in the German steel trading business, which has now been sold.
